A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NestedFP work. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support a reliable comparison after matching renamed and relocated content.

before.justification: V1 reports original accuracy measurements, GPU kernel and inference benchmarks, Azure trace analysis, and model-weight applicability statistics.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds accuracy measurements for two 70B models and a four-GPU SLO-attainment case study.

M1.justification: The reported NestedFP activation-quantization procedure changes from per-tensor scaling in v1 Section 5.1 to per-token scaling in v2 Section 5.1. The weight format, rounding, and FP16 reconstruction algorithm remain unchanged. Shortening the scheduling description does not establish that the earlier optimizations were removed from the implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions use Minerva Math, MMLU Pro, BBH, and Azure LLM serving traces; Appendix E analyzes the same model-weight collection. The additional 70B configurations and multi-GPU load study change models and protocols within the retained tasks, without establishing new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Torch FP8 is removed from the extended throughput comparison in Appendix C, although baseline FP8 remains in accuracy Table 2. CUTLASS FP16 and PyTorch/cuBLAS FP16 comparisons are retained, including the appendix comparison moved from D.2 to D.1.

E3.justification: V2 changes activation quantization and adds two 70B accuracy configurations. Main throughput testing changes from 256/512 to 1024/512 input/output tokens; Appendix C updates vLLM/PyTorch versions and specifies an 8192-token batching limit instead of adjusted limits. New Section 5.4 uses 1,000 requests, four H100 GPUs, a 1024-token switching threshold, and tight/loose SLO thresholds. Section 3 also changes the trace window and reports request-level violation percentages instead of violation durations.

E4.justification: V1 Section 5.2/Figure 7b's three-level kernel-optimization ablation is removed, including evidence for successive 38.3% and 11.0% latency reductions. V2 Section 5.4 adds a load-sweep case study testing SLO attainment. The extended GEMM-shape and weight-applicability analyses in Appendices B and E are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The latency percentiles and averages across configurations do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 revise existing accuracy entries and add two 70B model comparisons; for example, Mistral Nemo baseline FP8 Minerva accuracy changes from 16.9 to 16.5. New Table 3 reports 72.4% versus 0.7% tight-SLO attainment for NestedFP versus FP16 at 7.47 requests/s. Reported main FP16 overhead changes from 3.90% to 4.98%, and Appendix C from 3.88% to 5.52%, under revised settings rather than a demonstrated same-setting regression. FP8 throughput and optimization-ablation results are removed.

T1.justification: Equation 1, the weight-range assumption, fixed 2^8 scaling, and reconstruction relationships are retained. The rewritten explanations and reformatted algorithm introduce no substantive new mathematical definitions, proofs, or theoretical results.

C1.justification: V2 drops the headline claim of up to 1.55× FP8 speedup, revises the introductory FP16-overhead claim from 3.90% to 4.98%, and asserts FP8 throughput parity with native baselines. The central contributions—dual-precision inference with one FP16 memory footprint, preserved quality, and adaptive serving—remain.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly acknowledges that FP16 exception layers can reduce FP8 throughput benefits and qualifies its new SLO study through the simplicity of the switching policy, suggesting KV-cache-aware or predictive alternatives. It removes detailed explanations of scheduling optimizations and larger-model FP8 speedups. Appendix E's applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project code-access link and concrete implementation settings for the new SLO study. It updates throughput software and batching information and explicitly defines generated-token throughput. Conversely, it removes the CUTLASS 3.6 identifier and substantial kernel details, including advance-copy scheduling, the NVVM code-motion barrier, and register/shared-memory kernel discussion. The kernel search space is largely relocated rather than newly disclosed.

R1.justification: V2 adds model and benchmark sources, GPT-3/GPT-4 references, SOLA, and dynamic-length float compression, while removing Marlin and replacing its use as support for production-scale statistics. These additions improve attribution and context without substantially changing the work's positioning around FP8 quantization and dual-precision serving.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition, evaluation narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. V2 introduces explicit contribution and evaluation-result lists, Methodology/Results paragraphs, revised mode terminology, and a substantially condensed and reorganized Appendix D. These are widespread narrative changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V2 expands Table 2, adds the SLO table, redraws Figure 1 with an hourly trace and inset, and reformats v1 Figure 6 as Algorithm 1. It removes the optimization-ablation plot and two CUTLASS schematic figures, and redesigns throughput displays around FP16-only comparisons. These changes substantially alter the visual presentation beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The explicit NestedFP SLO study in Section 5.4/Table 3 and two additional 70B accuracy checks strengthen practical validation beyond v1's short motivational trace example. Clearer organization and code-access information also help. The net gain is limited by removal of the optimization ablation, direct FP8 throughput comparisons, and detailed kernel implementation explanations, which reduces diagnostic and reproducibility detail.
